original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Package the P104 banked-circuit toolkit (exact PRICEKIT pricer, stdlib word screens, banked-circuit fold/schedule/price core, independent circuit certifier, hub-reroute and causal-split screens and exact builders, pivot and relay screens) as one reviewable tool with a self-test on published words and circuits. No word and no kappa claim.
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card asks for a measured replay speed-up; this package ships the tooling behind #7705 and #7712 and its exact regression suite, including a stdlib mod-p word screen that runs a 154,768-event word in about 3 s, but makes no new performance claim. Recorded as changed.
bottleneck_link: Side result (tooling). Extending the banked P104 circuits needs the same exact pricer, certifier and move builders to be rerun on any published circuit; this makes the #7705/#7712 moves and checks reproducible by one command.
stop_rule: Keep the package only if tests/selftest.py reproduces every published number it wraps (#7700 crossing 0.00372934317806, #7712 crossing above 0.0037427697512), rejects its mutant and corrupted controls, and note-7717/check.py reproduces #7717's bracket from its published invoice; otherwise report the failing check instead of shipping.
evidence: VERIFY.json runs tests/selftest.py (asset pins, PRICEKIT closed-form and refusal controls, #7700 word crossing 0.00372934317806, word screens with two caught mutants, certify.py on the published #7712 circuit with Gaussian columns and a rejected corrupted control, hubbuild.py regression of two hub reroutes on #7712 accepted by certify.py) and note-7717/check.py (graph pin, hub rebuild equal to the stored diff, exact equality of all 1,470 outputs with #7717's graph, #7717 bracket reproduced, note crossing 0.00376346450049 on #7717's invoice plus the paid change; not a certificate of #7717's boundary).
author: DreamingOfClouds, with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), via Claude Code
ai_assistance: Prepared with Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code: Claude wrote and edited the tooling and tests under DreamingOfClouds' direction. Every command reproduces numbers published by the PRs it wraps or by exact recomputation; no independent human or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can the hub-reroute and split screens be made stdlib-only so that CI replays them?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The screens (hub2.py, split.py, search3.py) need numpy and are shipped as source; only the exact builders and certify.py run in CI.
open_questions.blocked_by: Dense mod-p kernels are written against numpy arrays.
open_questions.first_step: Port hub2.kernel and split.left_kernel to the sparse mod-p rows used by wordcheck.py and gate them against the numpy versions on #7712.

open_questions.question: Can certify.py check a circuit whose helper boundary differs from its source word, as in #7717?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The #7717 note is checked only by output equality with #7717's own graph; a boundary check would certify it directly.
open_questions.blocked_by: The helper-removal boundary (1,470 against 1,504 public roles) needs a stated identity map between removed helpers and the word.
open_questions.first_step: Read #7713's removal map as data and add a --boundary option that checks every retained output against the word.
